A walker's guide to the valley

First stretch of the valley

First stretch: The valley road follows the river for most of its length, and travellers rarely hurry along it. Farmers in the lower fields rotate their crops carefully, leaving one meadow fallow every third year. A small stone chapel stands at the first bend, and its bell is rung only on market days.

Second stretch of the valley

Second stretch: Children from the hamlets walk to the village school together, singing whenever the weather allows. Local cheese is aged in a cool cellar beneath the inn, where the air smells of oak and salt. In autumn the hills glow orange, and photographers arrive with tripods before dawn.

Third stretch of the valley

Third stretch: The postman knows every dog by name and carries biscuits in his left pocket. Winter closes the high pass, but the river keeps murmuring beneath a thin layer of ice. The valley road follows the river for most of its length, and travellers rarely hurry along it.
